sentences.text:
Satish Gangwal vs Ram Singh ,Food Inspector on 15 March,
2016
 1
 M.Cr.C.No.8502/2013
 Satish Gangwal Vs. Ramsingh & Others
15.03.2016
 Shri R.K. Sharma, counsel for the applicant.

Shri D.S. Tomar, counsel for respondents No.2&3.
 Shri Bps Chauhan, Public Prosecutor for respondent
No.4/State.
Heard on admission.

Applicant has preferred the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 against the order dated 20-09-2013 passed by learned 4 th Additional Sessions Judge, Vidisha in Criminal Appeal No.209/2010 whereby the application under Section 391 of Cr.P.C. filed by the applicant was dismissed.
 Facts of the case in short are that respondent No.1 -Food Inspector took a sample of chili powder from the shop of applicant which was run by the applicant in the name of "Mahavir Kirana Store Gulabganj".
It was informed by the applicant that the aforesaid chili powder was purchased by him from one Bhagwan Singh who was proprietor of "Kushwah Masala Udyog, Vidisha".

After considering the evidence adduced by the parties, the trial Court convicted the applicant for the offence under Section 7 read with Section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (in short 'the PF Act').

In appeal, the applicant has moved an application under Section 391 of Cr.P.C. that the respondents Bhagwan Singh and Brijmohan Kushwaha are real brother and they got a certificate of agmark for various items of Mahashakti Brand spices and he gave description of brothers of Bhagwan Singh who were partner of "Kushwah Masala Udyog" and according to Section 20-A of the PF Act, actual manufacturer of chili powder should have been punished and therefore, it was prayed that the certificate issued relating to agmark authorization dated 24-01-2011 be taken on record.
The State in its reply to the application has accepted the application, however the appellate Court vide order dated 20- 09-2013 has dismissed the application.

After considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the applicant relies upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of "Rambhau and another Vs. State of Maharashtra", {2001 SCC (Cri.) 812} in which condition has been laid by the Apex Court that when additional evidence can be taken at the appellate stage.

State of Gujarat and others" {2004 SCC (Cri.) 999} which is related to Articles 21 and 19 of the Constitution of India.

sentences.text:
Satish Gangwal vs Ram Singh ,Food Inspector on 15 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174514692/
1

For consideration of the application under Section 391 of Cr.P.C., it is for the appellate Court to consider as to whether the additional evidence which is to be produced would be helpful to the applicant for getting his acquittal.

In the present case, the applicant was found a seller of the adulterated chili powder and he immediately shown a bill that he purchased that chili powder from Manohar Traders, Vidisha which was run by Bhagwan Singh Kushwah.
If that chili powder was certified as agmark or otherwise then it was for Bhagwan Singh to move such application because by such evidence, applicant does not get any advantage in appeal.

He is basically a seller of chili powder who purchased the same from Bhagwan Singh and therefore, the evidence which is to be produced is not at all relevant for acquittal of the applicant in the appeal, hence the application filed by the applicant is not for adducing of additional evidence but it is for adding of extra accused persons in the case whereas he did not take such plea in his statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
No one can be permitted to move an application under Section 391 of Cr.P.C. to get the relief which may be obtained under Section 319 of Cr.P.C.

It was for the accused Bhagwan Singh to move an application under Section 319 during the trial if he had any grievance that he was not sole owner of the concerned company who sold the chili powder or who manufactured the same.

When it is stated that Bhagwan Singh was also partner of a particular company, it was for Bhagwan Singh to show that he purchased the chili powder from the aforesaid company who had authorization of agmark.
Possibility cannot be ruled out that Bhagwan Singh would have purchased the chili powder from someone else having bogus agmark of a particular manufacturer.

Hence, at this stage, when Bhagwan Singh did not apply for adding various accused persons under Section 319 of Cr.P.C.
before the trial Court, such application cannot be moved by the applicant under the garb of provisions of Section 391 of Cr.P.C.
When it is found that the additional evidence which is required to be produced before the appellate Court is not at all helpful to the applicant then such application having different object cannot be accepted.
The aforesaid judgments passed by the Apex Court are not at all helpful to the applicant for consideration of application under Section 391 of Cr.P.C.

The appellate Court has rightly rejected the application of the applicant under Section 391 of Cr.P.C.
because the application is not filed for the additional evidence but the object of the application is different.
The document which is to be filed is not at all helpful to the applicant for consideration of his appeal or conviction.

On the basis of aforesaid discussions, there is no any case in favour of the applicant so that the inherent power of this Court vested under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. can be invoked in favour of the applicant -Satish Gangwal.
Consequently, his petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. against the order dated 20-09-2013 passed by the appellate Court is hereby dismissed at motion stage.
Interim stay dated 09-10-2013 is hereby vacated.
Copy of the order be sent to the appellate Court for information and to proceed with appeal.

(N.K. Gupta) Judge Anil*
